meaning: From Egyptian Ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ ("House of the Ka of Ptah")

phonemes.desc: Initial sound of Aígyptos, as attested in the greek-location tradition.
Subsequent syllables preserve the name's inherited shape.

pronunciation.note: Aígyptos is Tier 1 because its Unicode restoration preserves the orthographic signature appropriate to the greek-location tradition.

domains.title: Personified Egypt, the Black Land
domains.subtitle: The domain of Aígyptos
domains.lead: In the greek location tradition, Aígyptos governed personified egypt, the black land. The name encodes a sphere of power that shaped ritual, narrative, and social order.

cards.title: Primary Sphere
cards.body: Aígyptos is principally associated with personified egypt, the black land.

cards.title: Cultural Role
cards.body: Worshippers approached Aígyptos through cult, myth, and the material culture of the greek-location world.

symbols.name: Ritual object
symbols.meaning: Material focus of devotion for Aígyptos

mythology.lead: The myths of Aígyptos preserve the name's power and personality across generations of retelling.

myths.title: The story of Aígyptos
myths.text: Aígyptos appears in greek location tradition as a figure whose domain over personified egypt, the black land shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Aígyptos's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Aígyptos in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Aígyptos carries within it a greek location understanding of from egyptian ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ ("house of the ka of ptah"). Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
